content: This pack teaches you to see inside
English words again — but the parts
are Greek, not Latin.
Long English words, especially in
science and medicine, are built by
joining Greek pieces together: a root,
a prefix, a suffix, or two roots
fused side by side.
Each card's Notes line also shows the
real Greek word in its own script,
like λόγος. You do not need to read
Greek — just learn to recognize it.
You are not memorizing a list. You
are learning a system. Start here.
Latin words often need a prefix and
a root. Greek is bolder: it will
often fuse two roots together with
nothing in between.
TELE means far. PHONE means sound.
tele + phone = telephone: sound
carried from far away.
GRAPH means write. tele + graph =
telegraph: writing sent from far
away.
Two roots you already half-know can
combine into a word you have never
seen. Read them in order and the
meaning is usually right there.
